newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen's Aden free zone attracts 457 projects.
newsitem.headline: Yemen's Aden free zone attracts 457 projects.

text.p: The Aden free zone in Yemen has received requests to start 457 investment projects at a cost of $1.16 billion, a member of the zone's board of directors said in remarks published on Thursday.

"By September the General Authority (of the zone) had received (requests for) 457 investment projects from different local, Arab and international investors and companies," Mohammed Saeed Dhafer, head of the zone's investment and orientation sector, told the 26th September weekly.
The 26th September is the official publication of the Yemeni armed forces.

"The implementation of these projects will cost $18.6 billion Yemeni rials ($186 million) plus $980 million," he said, as quoted by the paper. The cost was calculated in different currencies by local and international investors.

"The projects will be in different industrial, trade, tourism and housing sectors and in other fields and will create about 18,000 jobs," he said. Dhafar did not say when the projects would be implemented.
The $500 million Aden free zone, just outside the Red Sea's southern entrance, is expected to start operating in 1999.
